title: Software flags a red helmet in drone photographs of Monviso, and Piedmont mountain rescuers recover the body of a surgeon missing for ten months
summary: Image-analysis software, which its developer TEXSAR identifies as ADIAT, flagged a red helmet in about 2,600 drone frames, and rescuers recovered Nicola Ivaldo's body on Monviso by 31 July 2025.
account: Nicola Ivaldo was a surgeon aged 64, according to the Club Alpino Italiano's Lo Scarpone; another report says that he was 66. According to the Club Alpino Italiano, he disappeared on 14 September 2024 during a solo outing on Monviso in Piedmont, Italy. Quadricottero dates his departure, when he parked his car at the Pontechianale dam, to 15 September. Searches over ten months found nothing. On 29 July 2025 the Soccorso Alpino e Speleologico Piemontese (CNSAS) flew two drones close to the north face. They collected about 2,600 high-resolution frames over 183 hectares in five hours. AI image-analysis software analyzed the frames pixel by pixel and indicated three possible points of interest. The developer TEXSAR identifies the software as the open-source Automated Drone Image Analysis Tool (ADIAT), and the Club Alpino Italiano and CNSAS sources do not name it. One of the points was a tiny red anomaly in the Perotti couloir: his helmet. His body was located at about 3,150 m and recovered by 31 July 2025. Wired Italia, which TEXSAR's page cites, reports that the body was found on the morning of 31 July 2025. Bluewin reports that under 72 hours passed from the first drone flight to the recovery. The Club Alpino Italiano gives only July 2025, and Quadricottero gives no date. In January 2026 the Club Alpino Italiano reported that the drone lead of CNSAS Piemonte was working with the geomatics team of Politecnico di Torino on a successor tool. The new tool is meant to add precise georeferenced coordinates to the detection of color anomalies.
purpose: ADIAT was built to scan drone photographs and flag color and shape anomalies for search-and-rescue teams. Flagging the missing man's helmet was that intended function.
system: AI drone-image analysis software used by CNSAS Piemonte (identified as ADIAT by its developer, TEXSAR; CAI and CNSAS sources do not name it)
developer: TEXSAR (Texas Search and Rescue) volunteers, per the developer's own account
deployer: Soccorso Alpino e Speleologico Piemontese (CNSAS Piemonte), Turin station drone team
location: Monviso north face, Perotti couloir (province of Cuneo), Italy
segment: Recovery of a missing person in high-alpine terrain
taxonomy_note: The time cut is the rescuers' frame review; the family's good, recovery of remains, has no type.

ratings.reason: Ivaldo's family obtained the recovery of his body and certainty about his fate after ten months of searching. The search recovered a body, so no life was saved.

CNSAS Piemonte ended a ten-month search that had involved ground teams and helicopters of the Guardia di Finanza and the fire service. The Club Alpino Italiano says that manual analysis of the drone photographs would have taken weeks, and CNSAS told bluewin that it would have taken months.

ai_role.statement: The AI flagged a few red pixels, the helmet, a detail CAI describes as invisible to the naked eye. Ten months of helicopters, specialist teams and advanced technology (Quadricottero) had not resolved the search. Drone pilot Saverio Isola is quoted that it was the AI software that identified the differently colored pixels. CAI/CNSAS sources do not name the software. The ADIAT attribution comes from the developer TEXSAR's own page. So the tool identity rests on a vendor-authored source.

data.retained_case_account: Nicola Ivaldo was a surgeon aged 64 according to the Club Alpino Italiano's Lo Scarpone (another report says 66). He disappeared on 14 September 2024 per CAI during a solo outing on Monviso in Piedmont, Italy. Quadricottero dates his departure, when he parked his car at the Pontechianale dam, to 15 September. Searches over ten months found nothing. On 29 July 2025 the Soccorso Alpino e Speleologico Piemontese (CNSAS) flew two drones close to the north face. They collected about 2,600 high-resolution frames over 183 hectares in five hours. The frames were analyzed pixel by pixel with AI image-analysis software. Developer TEXSAR identifies it as the open-source Automated Drone Image Analysis Tool (ADIAT). The frames yielded a tiny red anomaly in the Perotti couloir: his helmet. fields.account: Nicola Ivaldo was a surgeon aged 64, according to the Club Alpino Italiano's Lo Scarpone; another report says that he was 66. According to the Club Alpino Italiano, he disappeared on 14 September 2024 during a solo outing on Monviso in Piedmont, Italy. Quadricottero dates his departure, when he parked his car at the Pontechianale dam, to 15 September. Searches over ten months found nothing. On 29 July 2025 the Soccorso Alpino e Speleologico Piemontese (CNSAS) flew two drones close to the north face. They collected about 2,600 high-resolution frames over 183 hectares in five hours. AI image-analysis software analyzed the frames pixel by pixel and indicated three possible points of interest. The developer TEXSAR identifies the software as the open-source Automated Drone Image Analysis Tool (ADIAT), and the Club Alpino Italiano and CNSAS sources do not name it. One of the points was a tiny red anomaly in the Perotti couloir: his helmet. His body was located at about 3,150 m and recovered by 31 July 2025. Wired Italia, which TEXSAR's page cites, reports that the body was found on the morning of 31 July 2025. Bluewin reports that under 72 hours passed from the first drone flight to the recovery. The Club Alpino Italiano gives only July 2025, and Quadricottero gives no date. In January 2026 the Club Alpino Italiano reported that the drone lead of CNSAS Piemonte was working with the geomatics team of Politecnico di Torino on a successor tool. The new tool is meant to add precise georeferenced coordinates to the detection of color anomalies.

value.text: The benefit is a one-time event: The body was located and recovered by 31 July 2025. By January 2026 the drone lead of CNSAS Piemonte was working with the geomatics team of Politecnico di Torino on a successor tool.

ratings.reason: Ivaldo's family obtained the recovery of his body and certainty about his fate after ten months of searching. The search recovered a body, so no life was saved.

CNSAS Piemonte ended a ten-month search that had involved ground teams and helicopters of the Guardia di Finanza and the fire service. The Club Alpino Italiano says that manual analysis of the drone photographs would have taken weeks, and CNSAS told bluewin that it would have taken months.

display.answer: The Club Alpino Italiano, the parent body of CNSAS, published two accounts of the case, and the developer TEXSAR published its own page. Eleven news reports and an OECD.AI incident entry cover the case, and one of the news reports dates from his disappearance in September 2024.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: Image-analysis software, which its developer TEXSAR identifies as ADIAT, flagged a red helmet in about 2,600 drone frames, and rescuers recovered Nicola Ivaldo's body on Monviso by 31 July 2025.
fields.account: Nicola Ivaldo was a surgeon aged 64, according to the Club Alpino Italiano's Lo Scarpone; another report says that he was 66. According to the Club Alpino Italiano, he disappeared on 14 September 2024 during a solo outing on Monviso in Piedmont, Italy. Quadricottero dates his departure, when he parked his car at the Pontechianale dam, to 15 September. Searches over ten months found nothing. On 29 July 2025 the Soccorso Alpino e Speleologico Piemontese (CNSAS) flew two drones close to the north face. They collected about 2,600 high-resolution frames over 183 hectares in five hours. AI image-analysis software analyzed the frames pixel by pixel and indicated three possible points of interest. The developer TEXSAR identifies the software as the open-source Automated Drone Image Analysis Tool (ADIAT), and the Club Alpino Italiano and CNSAS sources do not name it. One of the points was a tiny red anomaly in the Perotti couloir: his helmet. His body was located at about 3,150 m and recovered by 31 July 2025. Wired Italia, which TEXSAR's page cites, reports that the body was found on the morning of 31 July 2025. Bluewin reports that under 72 hours passed from the first drone flight to the recovery. The Club Alpino Italiano gives only July 2025, and Quadricottero gives no date. In January 2026 the Club Alpino Italiano reported that the drone lead of CNSAS Piemonte was working with the geomatics team of Politecnico di Torino on a successor tool. The new tool is meant to add precise georeferenced coordinates to the detection of color anomalies.
